devices.name: Metonymy
devices.definition: Naming something by a word closely associated with it — cause for effect, container for contents, author for writings.

occurrences.note: " Lest... thy labours be in the house of a stranger ": i.e., that which thou hast made or produced. So Ecc
" A young man void of heart ": i.e., of understanding. It is so used
" Righteousness delivereth from death ": i.e., from the things that end in death
" A righteous man knoweth the life of his beast ": i.e., he regardeth and careth for
" Hope deferred maketh the heart sick." Here, it is nut hope that is deferred, but the object hoped for. Jar
"The lips of knowledge": i.e., the words of wisdom, or wise words
"The words of a talebearer are as wounds, and they go down into the chambers of the belly ": i.e., the innermost thoughts and feelings, moving them as the belly is actually moved by excitement
"A foolish son is the calamity of his father ": i.e., does that which brings or produces calamity
" He that loveth (and therefore liveth in) pleasure shall be a poor man,"
" Apply thine heart (i.e., thy thoughts and powers) unto my knowledge."
" For the drunkard and the glutton shall come to poverty: and drowsiness (i.e., the sluggard) shall clothe a man (i.e., himself) with rags."
"When it giveth his eye (i.e., colour) in the cup."
" It is not good to know (or discern) faces in (giving) the judgment": i.e., to have respect or show favour to them
" He that trusteth in his own heart (i.e., understanding) is a fool."

devices.name: Idiom
devices.definition: A peculiar usage of the Hebrew or Greek that does not carry its literal force — an idiom to be rendered by its sense, not word for word.

occurrences.note: " a lion, strong among beasts ": i.e., the strongest of beasts. The New Testament has the same Idiom
" To do " for to bring to pass, do a very great deal, do all. So it is translated

devices.name: Paroemia (proverb)
devices.definition: A proverb — a wayside-saying in common use, cited or coined.

occurrences.note: " Surely in vain the net is spread in the sight of any bird."
" The prosperity of fools shall destroy them."
" For whom the Lord loveth He correcteth: even as a father the son in whom he delighteth." Here we have a Simile as well. It is referred to
" Go to the ant, thou sluggard: consider her ways and be wise."
" Can a man take fire in his bosom, and his clothes not be burned?" This is doubtless a saying arising from common observation of daily life
" He that gathereth in summer is a wise son."
"A rod is for the back of him who is void of understanding."
" The dog is turned to his own vomit again; And the sow that was washed to her wallowing in the mire." When we contrast this with
" Faithful are the wounds of a friend." Verse 7: " The full soul loatheth the honeycomb." Verse 17: "As iron sharpeneth iron,"

devices.name: Ellipsis
devices.definition: A word or words deliberately left out, to be supplied by the reader — compression and force.

occurrences.note: " If thou hast nothing to pay, why should one [i.e., the creditor] take away thy bed from under thee ? "
" He that saith unto the wicked, Thou art righteous; him shall the people curse, nations shall abhor him; " i.e., "He that saith to the wicked [king]-" This is clear from the context. Verses 21-25

devices.name: Synecdoche
devices.definition: Substituting a part for the whole, or the whole for a part (“all the world”; “flesh and blood”).

occurrences.note: "Feet (i.e., persons) that be swift in running to mischief."
"Blessings are upon the head of the just": i.e., upon the man himself
" A sound heart is the life of the flesh ": i.e., of the body
" Divers ephahs " are put for all kinds of measures
" Blessing" a friend with a loud voice, is put for all kinds of Hattery
" Feed me with food of my statute": i.e., my statutory food
"Open thy mouth for the dumb in the cause of all the sons of change." Here, the A.V. renders it in the margin " sons of destruction," and in the Text: " such as are appointed to destruction." 8

devices.name: Heterosis
devices.definition: Exchange of one grammatical form for another — of tense, number, person, degree, or mood (e.g. a future used for a command).

occurrences.note: " The scorners have delighted (i.e., will delight) in their scorning."
" So shalt thou find favour." Here the A.V. recognizes the figure, for the Heb. is imperative, " find." But the A.V. misses it
" And the wicked have been (i.e., will be) full of evil."

devices.name: Parallelism
devices.definition: Successive lines echo one another in structure — saying the same thing twice, or balancing matched clauses.

occurrences.note: " Faithful are the wounds of a friend. But deceitful are the kisses of an enemy " 3. Synthetic, or Constructive. This is where the parallelism consists only in the similar form of construction: —

devices.name: Anthropopatheia
devices.definition: Ascribing to God human feelings, parts, or actions, by way of condescension to us.

devices.name: Gnome (quotation)
devices.definition: A quotation or proverbial maxim woven in — a pithy saying cited for authority or point.

devices.name: Rhetorical question
devices.definition: A question asked for effect, not for an answer — to affirm, deny, or provoke thought.

devices.name: Tapeinosis
devices.definition: Deliberate understatement — belittling a thing to magnify it, or lessening to increase the effect.

occurrences.note: " A man shall not be established by wickedness: " i.e., he shall be overthrown
" The ants are a people not strong," i.e., very weak

devices.name: Anadiplosis
devices.definition: The word ending one clause is repeated to begin the next, linking them.

devices.name: Antimetabole
devices.definition: Words repeated in reverse order and grammatical relation (“sabbath for man … man for sabbath”).

devices.name: Paronomasia (wordplay)
devices.definition: A play on words that sound alike but differ in sense — pun, rhyme, near-repetition.

devices.name: Polyptoton
devices.definition: Repetition of the same root word in different inflections (“dying you shall die”).

devices.name: Synonymia
devices.definition: Amassing synonyms — words of like meaning — to enforce and enlarge a point.

devices.name: Acrostic
devices.definition: Successive lines or stanzas begin with the letters of the alphabet in order — a Hebrew form that cannot survive translation (Pss 25, 34, 119; Lam 1–4; Prov 31:10–31).

occurrences.note: perfect alphabetical Acrostic, marking and calling our attention to this song in praise of a virtuous woman

devices.name: Catachresis
devices.definition: One word used for another only remotely related — a deliberately incongruous transfer.

occurrences.note: When used with the word " mercies " itself, it denotes tender mercies

devices.name: Enigma
devices.definition: A dark saying — a truth wrapped in obscure or riddling terms.

devices.name: Epanorthosis
devices.definition: Recalling a word just used to correct or strengthen it (“not I, but the Lord”).

devices.name: Epizeuxis
devices.definition: Immediate repetition of a word for intense emphasis, with nothing between (“Lord, Lord”).

devices.name: Hypallage
devices.definition: Interchange: a word logically belonging to one term is grammatically attached to another.

occurrences.note: " Burning lips and a wicked heart are like a potsherd covered with silver of dross"-: i.e., dross of silver

devices.name: Hyperbole
devices.definition: Deliberate exaggeration, not meant literally, that drives a point home vividly.

devices.name: Metalepsis
devices.definition: A double metonymy: one word stands for a second, which itself stands for a third.

devices.name: Parechesis
devices.definition: Repetition of like-sounding words, especially from a foreign tongue — sound-play across languages.

devices.name: Periphrasis
devices.definition: Circumlocution: a description put in place of the plain name of a thing.

devices.name: Personification
devices.definition: Giving human traits, action, or speech to something impersonal or abstract.

occurrences.note: "The mouth of the just bringeth forth wisdom."

devices.name: Pleonasm
devices.definition: A deliberate redundancy — more words than strictly needed — to underline or solemnise.

occurrences.note: " Train up a child in the way he should go." Heb., in the mouth of his way: i.e., at the very mouth or entrance on life, so that it may be determined in a direction of justice and honesty
